p26.original: 非暴力沟通的第一个要素是观察。我们仔细观察正在发生的事情，并清楚地说出观察结果。非暴力沟通并不要求我们保持完全的客观而不作任何评论。它只是强调区分观察和评论的重要性。将观察和评论混为一谈，人们将倾向于听到批评，甚至会产生逆反心理。
p26.en: The first element of Nonviolent Communication is observation. We look closely at what is happening and say clearly the results of our observations. Nonviolent Communication does not require us to remain completely objective without comment. It simply emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between observations and comments. Confusion of observations and comments will tend to be critical and even counter-productive.

p27.original: 同时，非暴力沟通不鼓励绝对化的评论，而主张评论要基于特定时间和环境中的观察。语义学家温德尔·约翰逊（Wendell Johnson）认为，用静态的语言捕捉变动不居的现实，会造成许多困扰。他讲道：“我们的语言年代久远，但先天不足，是一种有缺陷的工具。它反映了万物有灵论的思想，让我们谈论稳定性和持久性，谈论相似之处、常态和种类，谈论神奇的转变、迅速的痊愈、简单的问题以及终极的解决办法。然而，我们的世界包含着无穷无尽的过程、变化、差别、层面、功能、关系、问题以及复杂性。静态的语言与动态的世界并不匹配，这是我们面临的挑战之一。”
p27.en: At the same time, Nonviolent Communication does not encourage absolute comments, but rather advocates that they be based on observations in a given time and context. Wendell Johnson, a semanticist, believes that capturing the changing reality in static language can cause many troubles. He said, “Our language is old, but innate, a flawed tool. It reflects the spiritual thinking of everything, and let us talk about stability and durability, about similarities, patterns and types, about magic transformations, quick healing, simple questions and ultimate solutions. However, our world encompasses endless processes, changes, differences, dimensions, functions, relationships, problems and complexities. Static language does not match the dynamic world, which is one of the challenges we face.

p70.original: 负面标签的消极影响很明显——例如用“懒惰”和“愚蠢”这样的词形容人。然而，正面或中性的标签也会妨碍我们全面了解一个人，例如用“厨师”一词定义人。
p70.en: The negative effects of negative labelling are evident — for example, in terms of “slazy” and “dumb”. However, positive or neutral labels also prevent us from fully understanding a person, for example by defining a person by the word “cooker”.

p71.en: The highest form of human intelligence

p72.original: 印度哲学家克里希那穆提（J.Krishnamurti）曾经说，“不带评论的观察是人类智力的最高形式。”第一次听到这个观点时，“胡说八道”这个想法在我脑中一闪而过——在不知不觉中，我作出了评论。对于大多数的人来说，观察他人及其行为，而不评判、指责或以其他方式进行分析，是难以做到的。
p72.en: As the Indian philosopher J. Krishnamurti once said, “observation without comment is the highest form of human intelligence. The first time I heard that idea, the idea of “bullshit” was flashing in my head — and I made comments without realizing it. For the majority of people, it is difficult to observe others and their behaviour without judging, accusing or otherwise analysing them.

p73.original: 在为一个小学提供咨询服务时，我对此有了深刻的体会。这个学校的教师和校长经常反映彼此很难沟通。于是，学区负责人请我协调双方的矛盾。我先和全体教师交谈，然后请校长来参加讨论。
p73.en: I have a deep sense of this in the provision of counselling services for a primary school. Teachers and principals of this school often reflect the difficulty of communicating with each other. So the school director asked me to reconcile the conflict. I spoke to all the teachers, and then I asked the headmaster to take part in the discussion.

p74.original: 会谈一开始，我就问：“校长的哪些行为不符合你们的需要？”“他是个大嘴巴。”有人马上回答。我的问题是想了解他们的观察——校长说了什么或做了什么，而“大嘴巴”只是这位教师对校长的评价。
p74.en: At the beginning of the meeting, I asked, “What are the principal's actions that do not fit your needs? "He's a big mouth." A response was received. My problem is to know their observations — what the principal said or did, and “Big Mouth” is the teacher's assessment of the principal.

p75.original: 在我指出这一点后，第二位教师补充说：“我知道他是什么意思。校长的话太多了！”这仍是一个评论——评论校长话多还是话少。随后，第三位教师说：“他认为只有他的话有价值。”我解释说，推测别人想什么与观察他的行为并不是一回事。最后，第四位教师也表明了看法：“他希望所有的人都一直听他讲话。”当我说这也是猜测时，有两位教师脱口而出：“你的问题真难回答啊！”
p75.en: After I pointed out this, the second teacher added: “I know what he means. The headmaster's got too much to say! “This is still a comment — more or less commented by the headmaster. The third teacher then said: “He thought that only his words were worth it. I explained that it was not the same thing to speculate about what others thought or to observe what he did. Finally, the fourth teacher also made a point: “He wants everyone to listen to him. When I said it was a guess, two teachers said, "You're a hard man to answer.

p76.original: 接着，我们注意区分观察和评论，一起列出了校长的具体行为。例如，在全体教员会议中，校长会讲他的童年和战时经历，有时导致会议超时20分钟。我问他们是否已向校长反映问题，他们说，他们试过，但从没有提及具体行为——例如校长在会议中回忆往事。最后，他们同意，在校长参加讨论时，指出这些行为。
p76.en: Then we look at the distinction between observations and comments, and together we list the specific behaviour of the headmaster. For example, during the plenary teacher's meeting, the headmaster spoke about his childhood and wartime experience, sometimes leading to meetings exceeding 20 minutes. I asked them whether they had addressed the questions to the headmaster, who said they had tried, but never mentioned specific acts — for example, the headmaster recalled the past in the meeting. Finally, they agreed to point out these acts when the headmaster participated in the discussion.

p77.original: 与校长的会谈开始后，我很快就发现教师们一直在说的事情。不论讨论的主题是什么，校长总是插话：“这让我想到……”然后，他就开始讲他的童年和战时经历。我等着教师们说出他们的不快。然而，他们运用的不是非暴力沟通，而是无声的抗议。一些人滴溜溜转着眼睛；另一些人故意打着哈欠；还有个人直盯着手表。
p77.en: I soon found out what the teachers were talking about when the meeting with the headmaster began. Whatever the theme of the discussion, the headmaster always interjects: “This reminds me of ” and then he starts talking about his childhood and his wartime experience. I'm waiting for the teachers to say they're not happy. However, they do not use Nonviolent Communication, but rather silent protests. Some people swipe their eyes; Some others were deliberately fighting a debt. There's someone staring at the watch.

p78.original: 我忍耐着这痛苦的场面，过了一会儿，我问道：“没有人有话要说吗？”接着是有些别扭的沉默。后来，在之前会谈中率先发言的那位教师鼓起勇气，冲着校长说：“你是个大嘴巴！”
p78.en: I endured this painful scene, and after a while, I said, "No one has anything to say? And then there was a bit of a bit of a bit of a little bit of silence. Later, the teacher who had been the first to speak at the previous meeting had the courage to say to the headmaster: “You are a big mouth!”

p79.original: 可见，不受旧习惯束缚，学会区分观察和评论，并不容易。最后，教师们终于告诉校长，他在做哪些事时，他们会感到不安。校长听后抱怨说：“为什么从没有人提醒我呢？”他承认他有讲故事的习惯。然而，他接着就开始说与这个习惯有关的故事！这时，我提醒了他。会谈结束时，我们总结了几个办法。一旦教师们不想听校长回忆往事，就温和地提醒他。
p79.en: It is therefore not easy to learn to distinguish between observations and comments without being bound by old customs. Finally, the teachers finally told the headmaster what he was doing and they were disturbed. The headmaster complained, "Why is there no one ever reminding me? He admits that he has a habit of telling stories. And then he starts telling stories about this habit! And then I reminded him. At the end of the talks, we summarized a few approaches. Once the teachers do not want to hear the headmaster's memory, they kindly remind him.

p97.original: 非暴力沟通的第一个要素是观察。将观察和评论混为一谈，别人就会倾向于听到批评，并反驳我们。非暴力沟通是动态的语言，不主张绝对化的结论。它提倡在特定的时间和情境中进行观察，并清楚地描述观察结果。例如，它会说“欧文在过去的5场比赛中没有进一个球”，而不是说“欧文是个差劲的前锋”。
p97.en: The first element of Nonviolent Communication is observation. When observations and comments are confused, others tend to listen to criticisms and counter them. Nonviolent Communication is a dynamic language that does not favour absolute conclusions. It promotes observation at certain times and contexts and clearly describes the results of observation. For example, it would say, “Irving didn't win a ball in the past five games”, rather than “Irving was a bad front”.

p99.original: “我们遇到的最傲慢的演讲者”
p99.en: "The most arrogant speaker we've ever met."

p100.original: 以下的对话来自我主持的一个研讨班。在讲解了半小时后，我停下来请学员反馈意见。这时，有个人举起了手，他说：“你是我们遇到的最傲慢的演讲者！”
p100.en: The following dialogue comes from a workshop that I hosted. After an hour and a half, I stopped to ask for feedback from the participants. At that point, a man raised his hand and said, "You are the most arrogant speaker we've ever met!

p101.original: 如果有人这样对我说话，我的反应有几种可能。其中之一是认为自己确实有问题。我知道，一旦我想为自己辩护或开脱，我就默认了自己有问题。另一种反应是把对方的话视为攻击而给予反击。这一次，我既没有辩解也没有指责对方，而用心理解为什么他会这么说。
p101.en: If someone talks to me like that, there are several possibilities for my reaction. One of them is to think that there is a real problem. I know that once I wanted to defend myself or excuse myself, I acquiesced in my own problems. Another response was to counter-attack the other side's words as an attack. This time, I have neither justified nor accused each other, but I understand why he would say that.

p103.original: 我：（猜测他的观察结果）“你这么说，是针对我讲了半小时才请你们发表意见？”
p103.en: And I said, "Well, I guess his observations, "You said it was half an hour before I asked you to comment?

p104.original: 他：“不是。是因为你把事情说得太简单了。”
p104.en: He said, "No. It's because you make things so simple.

p105.original: 我：（请他澄清）“那么，针对的是，我没有说有些人可能难以运用这个模式？”
p105.en: I: “Please clarify, then, I do not say that some people may have difficulty applying this model?

p106.original: 他：“不，不是有些人，而是你自己！”
p106.en: He said, "No, not some, but yourself!

p107.original: 我：“那么，你这么说是针对我没有提到有时我也很难运用这个模式？”
p107.en: And I said, "So, you're saying that to me, and you don't mention that sometimes I can't use this model, either?

p109.original: 我：“你感到不高兴是因为你希望我在前面的讲演中提到我的困难？”
p109.en: I said, "You're upset because you wanted me to mention my difficulties in my previous speech?

p111.original: 我：（了解他的感受和需要后，我开始关注他的请求。）“你希望我现在就承认有时我也很难运用这个模式？”
p111.en: I: I began to follow up on his request, knowing his feelings and needs. "Do you want me to admit now that sometimes it's hard for me to use this model?

p113.original: 我：（了解他的观察、感受、需要和请求后，我问自己是否愿意满足他的请求。）“是的，使用这个模式，我经常会遇到困难。在这个研讨接下来的时间里，你也许会听到我介绍我遇到的几次困难……有时甚至是完全忘记我刚才提及的模式……是什么使我继续努力运用它呢？那是因为一旦我成功运用它，我与他人的感情就加深了。”
p113.en: I asked myself if I would be willing to meet his request, after learning about his observations, feelings, needs and requests. “Yes, I've often had difficulties using this model. In the coming days of this discussion, you may hear me describe a few of the difficulties I have encountered... and sometimes even completely forget the pattern I have just mentioned... What makes me continue my efforts to use it? That's because once I've used it successfully, my feelings with others have deepened.
